body:
### Description

`SessionAffinity.get` returns `parentID ?? fork?.sessionID ?? id`, and `fork.sessionID` is the session a fork was made from, not the root. So in a chain P → M → G, M sends `prompt_cache_key` = P, but G sends M, a key nothing was ever sent under. G's first request writes the whole prompt again although its prefix is the same as P's and M's.

#51923 describes the affinity as "the parent ID, then the fork root", and `model-request.ts` already has `// TODO: Persist cache lineage so nested forks reuse the root session's cache key.` Filing it because the cost is a full prompt write for every fork of a fork.

Measured with openai/gpt-6.1-sol, a ~5.7k-token file loaded in P:

| Request | Key | Cached tokens |
|---|---|---|
| fork of P | P | 5,504 |
| first fork of that fork | M | 0 |
| second fork of that fork | M | 5,632 |
| fork of P with the same messages as G | P | 5,504 |

Nested subagents (`experimental.subagent_depth` > 1) have the same gap through `parentID`: a grandchild sends its parent's id, while the parent sends the root.

PR follows: walk `parentID` / `fork.sessionID` up to the root when the request is built, the way the subagent tool already walks `parentID` for its depth limit. No schema change. The provider plugins (`openai.ts`, `chatgpt.ts`, `github-copilot.ts`) call `SessionAffinity.get` for their session headers, so they get the same root.

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e9def88a7790efc6abace15b67f3625ff4d66237/packages/core/src/session/affinity.ts#L6-L8
